demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors.

demos.heading: Architecture: the path a claim takes, station by station
demos.purpose: The cell cuts the handbook with the kit's chunker, takes NP-03, the notice-period clause, and holds six quotes against it with quote_holds(): the sentence as written, a sentence that crosses a line break, the same sentence with revision 2's figure, a paraphrase, the whole clause, and the whole clause as _draft() trims an over-long quote. Each line prints both halves of the rule and the kit's verdict.

demos.heading: Cost: a claim, a month and a floor, at 1k, 10k and 100k claims
demos.purpose: This is the table as a script you can keep: component 6's COST-MODEL.md starts from its output. It reads the rates and the rupee rate from the kit, rebuilds a claim's budget with the kit's own function, and carries the three prices the kit does not hold, the embedding, the ranking query and the judge's autorater, as constants with their date. The ceiling is what no claim may exceed; the average is what claims cost. make usage reads the last day's usage rows, and its table by model and backend carries each model's answers and tokens; the second line divides them. Your average depends on what was asked on your lane, so it is yours, not the author's.
